findings.claim: First-exception-wins is only trivially verified: in every configuration, PrimaryStable is unfalsifiable because no reachable behavior can attempt to overwrite st.primary with a DIFFERENT error value.
findings.evidence: MC_Fail.tla sets mc_FailLeaves == {1} and mc_FaultySteps == {"scan", "pre"}; the only distinct error values are eL1 (FaultProbe on leaf 1, probe phase only) and efault (FaultScan/FaultStep, active/pre phases only). These phases are mutually exclusive for pending faults: OwnershipConsistent (WaveJoinProbe.tla:669-676) forces owned jobs into ExistingJobs of the CURRENT phase, Seal (line 281) requires all reservations landed before pre, and PreBarrier/ScatterBarrier/... are ~cancelled-guarded so after any efault fault the probe phase is unreachable, and in probe phase no scan/pre job can be owned. The only reachable concurrent double faults are pre+pre or scan+scan, both writing the identical FaultError, so the IF st.primary = NoError guard (lines 463, 472, 481) can never be observed doing anything, and PrimaryStable (line 830) cannot fail. In MC_Normal/MC_PL1/MC_MultiWave, FailLeaves = {} and FaultySteps = {} make PrimaryStable fully vacuous. This is the same hidden-vacuity pattern the contract banned for F1, now on the failure path; MC_Fail's 4,385 generated / 1,852 distinct states (test_wave_join_tla.log:41) reflect this shallow fault space.
findings.suggested_fix: In tmp/wave-join-cooperative/tla/MC_Fail.tla set mc_FailLeaves == {1, 3} (mc_ErrorOf already yields distinct values eL1 vs eOther, and both leaves are populated by hashes 1 and 3 of block 1). With WORKERS = 2, both workers can concurrently own ProbeJob(1) and ProbeJob(3) and fault in either order, so any overwrite of primary produces a PrimaryStable counterexample. Verify the fix is live by temporarily removing the IF st.primary = NoError guard from FaultProbe and confirming TLC reports the violation.

findings.claim: No configuration injects a fault during scatter, refalloc, or refine, although the spec explicitly supports it; the fault-unwind path from those phases (requirement 8: injected failure with owned-work unwind) is never model-checked.
findings.evidence: WaveJoinProbe.tla:66 declares FaultySteps over {"scan","pre","scatter","refalloc","refine"} and FaultStep (lines 465-472) handles all of them, but MC_Fail.tla sets mc_FaultySteps == {"scan", "pre"} and every other config sets {}. Consequently FaultStep releasing a ScatterJob (leaving a block unscattered with liveEntries still live), a RefAllocJob (leaving liveA1 partially allocated across passes), or a RefineJob (leaving arena1 partially filled) is dead code in the checked state space; Teardown's handling of those live sets under a fault (as opposed to an external cancel, which MC_Fail does reach in those phases) is unverified.
findings.suggested_fix: Extend MC_Fail (or add an MC_Fail2 config) with mc_FaultySteps == {"scan", "pre", "scatter", "refalloc", "refine"} and re-run the gate; the input is small enough that the state-space growth is negligible.

findings.claim: Exactly-once release of the leaf arenas (arena1) is asserted in a comment but not independently verified: there is no freedA1 counter, and liveA1 is a set, so a double release would be idempotent and invisible to every checked invariant.
findings.evidence: The comment at FinishProbe (WaveJoinProbe.tla:417-418) says 'The leaf arena is released exactly once, here', but the release is modeled only as liveA1 = @ \ {l} (line 426, also FaultProbe line 482) and Teardown clears liveA1 without any accounting (line 524). FreedOnce (lines 746-748) covers only freedEntries and freedA0. The entries/A0 resources got dual-path freed counters precisely because two actions can free them (ScatterBarrier/RefineBarrier vs Teardown); arena1 has the same dual-path structure (FinishProbe/FaultProbe vs Teardown) yet no counter, so requirement 8's 'exactly-once release' is checked for two of the three resource classes only — a future edit that releases a leaf twice cannot produce a counterexample.
findings.suggested_fix: Add freedA1 \in [Leaves -> Nat] (or a bag), incremented by FinishProbe, FaultProbe, and by Teardown for each l \in liveA1 at teardown time; strengthen FreedOnce with \A l \in Leaves : st.freedA1[l] <= 1 and add a terminal check that every allocated leaf was freed exactly once.

findings.claim: Cancellation never races normal completion and no failure/cancellation is ever exercised after a completed wave: the interleavings 'cancel after probeDone = Leaves but before CompleteWave', 'cancel just before FinishInput/EOFSeal', and 'fault or cancel during wave 2 with doneWaves non-empty' are unreachable in every configuration.
findings.evidence: MC_Fail is the only config with CancelAllowed = TRUE or non-empty faults, but its FailLeaves = {1} with a populated leaf 1 makes FinishProbe(w, 1) permanently disabled (WaveJoinProbe.tla:421), so st.probeDone = Leaves and hence CompleteWave (line 428) and phase "done" are unreachable there; its input (2 blocks of 1 byte, BUDGET = 2) also yields exactly one wave, so Teardown with st.doneWaves # <<>> never occurs. MC_Normal/MC_PL1/MC_MultiWave complete but have CancelAllowed = FALSE and no faults. Requirement 8 demands modeling normal completion AND cancellation under the same machine; the boundary states where they interact (Teardown after all resources already freed at a wave boundary, TerminalClean's failed-branch with complete per-worker output) are never generated.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a config (e.g. MC_CancelRace) with CancelAllowed = TRUE, FailLeaves = {}, FaultySteps = {} and a 3-4 block input producing two waves; check the full safety battery plus a disjunctive termination property <>(st.phase \in {"done", "failed"}). This makes cancel race Seal, CompleteWave, FinishInput, and the second wave's drain.

findings.claim: The gate wrapper claims every positive configuration checks the full safety battery but textually enforces only FinalRefinement, so a silently weakened .cfg (e.g. RaceFree or FreedOnce deleted) would still turn the gate green.
findings.evidence: verify_tla.sh header (lines 11-13) states 'Every positive configuration checks the full safety battery', but the only content check is the FinalRefinement grep loop (lines 63-69) over three cfgs; TLC itself reports 'No error' regardless of how few invariants a cfg lists, and the PASS criterion (line 84) is just that string. Today the four positive cfgs do list all 19 invariants, so this is a drift/soundness hole in the gate, not a current miss.
findings.suggested_fix: Extend the textual step to diff the INVARIANTS block of each positive cfg against the canonical list (e.g. the conjuncts of Safety extracted from WaveJoinProbe.tla, or a hard-coded list), failing the gate on any missing invariant or missing PROPERTIES entry (Termination/ParticipationLive/PrimaryStable).

findings.claim: The header maps `Reserve`/`Admit` to an "atomic fetch-add on the wave byte counter" (src/Interpreters/RadixHashJoin/WaveJoinProbe.tla lines 27-28, also lines 7-8), but `Reserve` (lines 250-262) models a strictly stronger primitive — an atomic conditional add (check `st.mem < BUDGET` and increment in one action). A literal fetch-add implementation admits counter states the model excludes by construction, so the TLC-verified `MemBound` (line 639) and the header claim "mem <= BUDGET + MaxBlockBytes always" (lines 41-42) do not transfer to the documented primitive, and the rejected-reservation rollback obligation is unmodeled and therefore unverified.
findings.evidence: In the spec, `Reserve` is enabled only when `st.mem < BUDGET`, so once the counter crosses BUDGET no lane can ever add to it again — there is no state in which a losing lane has inflated the counter. With a real `fetch_add` (add unconditionally, then inspect the returned old value), a lane whose old value is >= BUDGET has already added its bytes and must compensate with a `fetch_sub`; during that window the physical counter reaches up to BUDGET + MaxBlockBytes + (WORKERS-1)*MaxBlockBytes, exceeding the modeled bound `MemBound == st.mem <= BUDGET + MaxBlockBytes` for any WORKERS >= 2. No action in the spec represents "reservation rejected, bytes rolled back", so an implementation bug in that path (missing or double rollback, or a `Seal` that evaluates the every-in-flight-admitted condition against the transiently inflated counter) is invisible to every configuration in tmp/wave-join-cooperative/tla/ — the gate (build/reldeb/test_wave_join_tla.log) is green while proving bounds for a primitive the implementation is not documented to use. The reachability witness MC_ReachInflight/MC_ReachCross exercise concurrent reservations but only ever below-budget ones, confirming the rejected-add state is unreachable in the model.
findings.suggested_fix: Align the mapping and the model. Either (a) fix the mapping comment (lines 27-28 and 7-8) to state that the reservation is an atomic conditional add (CAS loop: retry `cur -> cur + bytes` only while `cur < BUDGET`), making that the binding implementation contract; or (b) keep the fetch-add mapping and extend the model with the rejected-reservation transient: a `ReserveRejected(w)` action that adds `Bytes(b)` when `st.mem >= BUDGET`, followed by a mandatory exactly-once rollback action before the worker becomes idle, restating `MemBound` as admitted+in-flight-admissible bytes <= BUDGET + MaxBlockBytes while bounding the physical counter separately by BUDGET + WORKERS*MaxBlockBytes, and making `Seal` insensitive to rejected in-flight bytes. Option (a) is the minimal change and keeps the current invariants sound.

findings.claim: `MemAccounted` (src/Interpreters/RadixHashJoin/WaveJoinProbe.tla lines 636-637) is scoped to `st.phase # "failed"`, but the unscoped equality `st.mem = SumBytes(st.queue) + InflightBytes` provably holds in the "failed" phase too; the exclusion weakens the checked theorem for no reason and falsely implies that the failure path desynchronizes the byte accounting.
findings.evidence: TLC run on MC_Fail (the configuration with FailLeaves = {1}, FaultySteps = {"scan","pre"}, CancelAllowed = TRUE) with the antecedent removed: "Model checking completed. No error has been found." (4385 states, identical state count to the gate run in build/reldeb/test_wave_join_tla.log). This is expected from the actions: `Teardown` (lines 514-524) touches neither `mem` nor `queue`, and its guard `\A w : st.wk[w].stopped` together with `OwnershipConsistent` conjunct 4 (lines 675-676) forces `InflightBytes = 0`, while `FaultScan` (lines 455-463) and `ReleaseRes` (lines 498-503) subtract bytes and clear `res` in the same action. The scope hides no violation — it merely under-claims. (By contrast, the `~st.cancelled` scope on `CrossedSound`, lines 641-643, is genuinely necessary: removing it produces "Error: Invariant CrossedSound is violated" on MC_Fail via a fault-released crossing reservation, and that excluded state is harmless because `Seal` requires `~st.cancelled` at line 283 and cancellation is irreversible.)
findings.suggested_fix: Drop the `st.phase # "failed" =>` antecedent from `MemAccounted` so the strongest true accounting invariant is the one the gate checks, and note in the adjacent F5 comment (lines 633-635) that in "failed" the counter still equals the accounted bytes even though `Teardown` has released the underlying entries (`liveEntries` cleared, `freedEntries` bumped) — i.e. the counter is abandoned, not desynchronized.

result.reasoning: The claim's mechanics are accurate: verify_tla.sh's only textual content check is the FinalRefinement grep (lines 63-69) and the positive PASS criterion is TLC's "No error" string (line 84), so a future silent deletion of an invariant from a .cfg would not by itself turn the gate red. However, the finding fails the realness bar. (1) No binding-contract clause is violated: item 6 (FinalRefinement checked by a successful config) is satisfied and textually enforced; item 3 (non-vacuous participation) is enforced dynamically by the MC_NoSteal negative witness, which is stronger than any grep; nothing in the contract requires the gate to diff cfg INVARIANTS blocks against the Safety conjuncts. (2) No vacuity is hidden today: all four positive cfgs list all 19 conjuncts of Safety (WaveJoinProbe.tla lines 768-787) plus the three PROPERTIES, and the green log (build/reldeb/test_wave_join_tla.log) shows all positives completing and all witnesses failing as required — the claim itself concedes "not a current miss." (3) The header (lines 11-13) is a true description of the current cfgs and explicitly scopes textual verification to FinalRefinement, so the wrapper does not overclaim. The cited behavior is hypothetical future drift, and any anti-drift grep is itself equally editable; the gate already cmp-verifies the spec copy (line 49). This is a defensible hardening suggestion, not a contract violation or hidden vacuity.

The cited facts are accurate (FaultySteps declared over five steps at WaveJoinProbe.tla:66, FaultStep at lines 465-472 handles all of them, MC_Fail.tla checks only {"scan","pre"}, other configs {}), but the conclusion is refuted by the spec text. FaultStep mutates only wk[w].job, wk[w].stopped, cancelled, and primary — it touches no live sets, arenas, mem, or done-sets. MC_Fail runs with CancelAllowed = TRUE, and ExternalCancel + ReleaseJob + StopWorker in the scatter/refalloc/refine phases produces states identical to a FaultStep fault in those phases in every variable except primary. Therefore Teardown's handling of a partially-scattered liveEntries, partially-allocated liveA1, and partially-filled arena1 IS verified in the checked state space (Teardown never reads primary), contradicting the finding's core claim that this unwind path is unverified. The only unreached states are primary = FaultError during those three phases, and the primary logic (FailureSafety, PrimaryStable write-once via the phase-independent guard at line 472) is exercised in MC_Fail by scan-, pre-, and probe-phase faults including first-exception-wins races. Requirement 8 asks that injected failure and cancellation be modeled and checked — both are — and does not mandate fault injection in every drain step; MC_Fail's header documents the scan/pre choice. Extending mc_FaultySteps would pass trivially (barriers are ~cancelled-guarded, so no double-free interaction with FreedOnce exists to expose) and adds only future-proofing against edits to FaultStep's currently-dead branches. That makes this a cheap coverage-hardening suggestion, not a contract violation, hidden vacuity, or soundness hole.

Cited lines are accurate (FinishProbe comment at WaveJoinProbe.tla:417-418, set-removal releases at 426/482, Teardown clearing liveA1 at 524, FreedOnce covering only freedEntries/freedA0 at 746-748), but the finding does not rise to a contract failure, hidden vacuity, or soundness hole. (1) No reachable behavior double-releases a leaf arena: releases occur only in FinishProbe/FaultProbe under job ownership; the CHECKED invariant OwnershipConsistent (owned job must be in ExistingJobs, which excludes probeDone) plus cancelled => UnownedClaimable = {} makes re-acquisition of ProbeJob(l) impossible, and Teardown frees only the still-live remainder. The finding itself only argues about a hypothetical future edit — mutation-robustness of instrumentation, not a defect in the spec as written. (2) The per-leaf exactly-once discipline is non-vacuously checked through another channel: FinishProbe's release is atomic with result emission, so the only structurally plausible double-release (re-executing ProbeJob(l)) duplicates output and violates OutputJustified/FinalRefinement, which use duplicate-sensitive multiset counting (MC_MultiWave deliberately includes duplicate result values). (3) The claimed asymmetry with entries/A0 is weaker than stated: Teardown increments freedEntries/freedA0 only when the corresponding live set is non-empty (lines 520-521), so those counters are conditioned on the same live-set state and would also not catch the analogous 'Teardown after barrier' double-free under a hostile edit; they mainly encode that a bulk-free barrier fires once per wave, which has no per-leaf analogue other than probeDone (already cross-checked by OwnershipConsistent and the output multiset). (4) The live-set resource abstraction is documented in the spec (Teardown comment lines 512-513) and is a standard, defensible TLA+ idiom where exactly-once release is a consequence of checked ownership invariants rather than a dedicated counter. Adding freedA1 would be a reasonable hardening, but requirement 8 is satisfied and verified non-vacuously in every green configuration; nothing checked passes vacuously because of the missing counter.

findings.claim: ParticipationLive is logically implied by Termination under this spec, so it adds zero discriminating power in every configuration where it is checked, and the cooperative-participation half of the contract (requirements 2/3) is still verified only by definition (ClaimEligible == TRUE), not by any property that could fail on a work-conserving dedicated-crew design.
findings.evidence: src/Interpreters/RadixHashJoin/WaveJoinProbe.tla lines 821-826: ParticipationLive's eventuality has escape disjuncts `(UnownedClaimable = {} /\ ~ScanOpen)` and `st.cancelled`. At phase = "done", ExistingJobs = {} (line 186 OTHER branch) and ScanOpen is false (line 809 requires phase = "active"), so the escape holds; at phase = "failed", st.cancelled holds (TerminalClean line 760). Hence every behavior satisfying Termination (line 801) satisfies ParticipationLive: a counterexample must be a non-terminating wedge, which Termination already catches. Consequently the property misses every broken design the lens enumerates that still completes: a lazy worker whose work others consume, static partitioning with live owners, and sealer-drains-alone all reach "done" and pass. The MC_NoSteal witness (tmp/wave-join-cooperative/tla/MC_NoSteal.tla lines 31-35) is an honest falsification and -deadlock in verify_tla.sh line 98 is legitimate, but its comment "it fails exactly on dedicated-crew designs" overclaims: broken_ClaimEligible makes ProbeJob(0) claimable by NOBODY (worker 0 excluded from all claims AND leaf 0 denied to w # 0), i.e. it fails only on orphaned-work designs, which equally violate Termination. The contract's letter (capable of failing, compares ExistingJobs-derived work against wk-derived ownership) is met, but the F1 remediation produced a property redundant with an already-checked one.
findings.suggested_fix: Give the participation check content orthogonal to Termination: e.g. add reachability witnesses in the gate that every worker id actually executes drain jobs in some behavior (a Never-style invariant such as `NeverWorkerNProbes == \A l : ProbeJob-not-finished-by-worker-N`, expected violated, per worker), and/or state a per-worker property without the consumed-by-others escape, checked in a config where it is non-trivial. At minimum, correct the MC_NoSteal and spec-header comments to say the property verifies no-orphaned-work (work conservation), not per-worker cooperation, and note it is implied by Termination.

findings.claim: Exactly-once release (contract requirement 8) is verifiable for input entries and pass arenas but not for leaf arenas: liveA1 has no freed counter, and set-based removal makes a double release a state no-op that no invariant in the battery can ever detect.
findings.evidence: src/Interpreters/RadixHashJoin/WaveJoinProbe.tla: FreedOnce (lines 746-748) bounds only st.freedEntries and st.freedA0; those counters are incremented at ScatterBarrier (lines 361, 367), RefineBarrier (line 413) and Teardown (lines 520-521), which is what makes a hypothetical double free of entries/pass-arenas fail FreedOnce. Leaf arenas by contrast are released via bare set difference — FinishProbe line 426 `!.liveA1 = @ \ {l}`, FaultProbe line 482 `!.liveA1 = @ \ {l}`, Teardown line 524 `!.liveA1 = {}` — with no freedA1 counter. Removing an already-removed element leaves the state unchanged, so an erroneous transition releasing a leaf arena twice (e.g. a Teardown variant that frees leaves already freed by FinishProbe, or FaultProbe firing on an already-released leaf) is invisible to every checked invariant. The exactly-once machinery exists precisely because of the earlier vacuity findings, and it silently does not cover one of the three resource classes.
findings.suggested_fix: Model leaf release the same way as the other resources: add `freedA1 \in [Leaves -> Nat]` (or a per-leaf counter), increment it in FinishProbe, FaultProbe and Teardown (for leaves still in liveA1), and extend FreedOnce with `\A l \in Leaves : st.freedA1[l] <= 1`, resetting it in CompleteWave.

findings.claim: RaceFree is vacuously true for every cross-kind job pair touching arena0 because Footprint encodes pre/refine access as <<"a0", p>> but scatter access as <<"a0cell", Pid, Rank0>>, keys that can never intersect; all cross-kind write-range exclusion is silently delegated to OwnershipConsistent's phase-keyed ExistingJobs.
findings.evidence: src/Interpreters/RadixHashJoin/WaveJoinProbe.tla lines 678-687: Footprint(PreJob(p)) = {<<"a0", p>>} and Footprint(RefineJob(p)) includes <<"a0", p>>, while Footprint(ScatterJob(b)) = {<<"a0cell", Pid(o), Rank0(...)>> : ...}. A 2-tuple tagged "a0" never equals a 3-tuple tagged "a0cell", so RaceFree (lines 689-694) reports disjoint footprints for a pre or refine job racing a scatter job over the same pass arena. Today such co-ownership is unreachable (OwnershipConsistent conjunct 2, lines 672-673, confines owned jobs to the current phase's ExistingJobs), so the mismatch is dead — but that means RaceFree's cross-kind clause checks nothing, and if the phase structure were ever relaxed (pipelined pre/scatter), TLC would spuriously report the race-free invariant satisfied. This is checked-invariant vacuity hidden behind an unreachable case.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the arena0 footprint keys collide where the writes collide: give PreJob(p) and RefineJob(p) the full cell set {<<"a0cell", p, i>> : i \in ...} (or give scatter an additional <<"a0", Pid(o)>> element per touched pass), so RaceFree would genuinely fail on any cross-kind overlap should phase separation ever be weakened.

findings.claim: Fault injection never exercises the scatter, refalloc, or refine drain steps in any configuration, so FaultStep abandoning a mid-drain job (job released, done-set NOT updated, primary = FaultError, unwind through Teardown from those phases) is model-checked only for the "pre" step, despite the spec allowing all five sites.
findings.evidence: src/Interpreters/RadixHashJoin/WaveJoinProbe.tla line 583 permits FaultySteps \subseteq {"scan", "pre", "scatter", "refalloc", "refine"}, but the only fault-injecting configuration, tmp/wave-join-cooperative/tla/MC_Fail.tla, sets `mc_FaultySteps == {"scan", "pre"}`; MC_Normal/MC_PL1/MC_MultiWave/MC_NoSteal all set `mc_FaultySteps == {}`. ExternalCancel (CancelAllowed = TRUE in MC_Fail) does reach the scatter/refalloc/refine phases, but always with primary = NoError, so the combination "first exception raised while a scatter/refalloc/refine job is in flight" and the resulting FaultStep unwind (WaveJoinProbe.tla lines 465-472) in those phases is unexplored state space; the gate's claim of fault coverage (verify_tla.sh line 10, "probe fault, scan/pre faults") is accurate but narrower than the modeled fault surface.
findings.suggested_fix: Extend mc_FaultySteps in MC_Fail to {"scan", "pre", "scatter", "refalloc", "refine"} (state count stays small — MC_Fail currently explores only ~1.9k distinct states), or add a second failure configuration covering the remaining sites.

result.reasoning:
CONFIRMED. The claimed hidden vacuity is real and every step of the offered evidence checks out against the actual text.

(1) Error-value inventory is correct: in MC_Fail.tla (lines 20-24) the only fault actions are FaultProbe on leaf 1 (writes ErrorOf(1)="eL1", probe phase only) and FaultScan/FaultStep (write FaultError="efault", active/pre phases only). "eOther" is defined but unreachable because mc_FailLeaves == {1}.

(2) Phase exclusivity is real, and machine-verified, not just plausible: OwnershipConsistent (WaveJoinProbe.tla:669-676, green in the gate run) forces any owned job into ExistingJobs of the CURRENT phase (probe jobs only in phase "probe", pre jobs only in "pre") and forces res#NoBlock => phase="active"; no job has kind "scan" at all, so FaultStep only fires on pre jobs. Every fault sets cancelled=TRUE, and Claim (via UnownedClaimable, line 191), Reserve/Admit, all barriers, and CompleteWave are ~cancelled-guarded, so after the first fault the phase freezes and no new ownership arises. Therefore: after efault (active/pre) the probe phase is unreachable (no later eL1); after eL1 (probe) no reservation or pre job can exist (no later efault). The only reachable second faults are scan+scan and pre+pre, both writing the identical "efault" over "efault", and probe+probe is impossible (single failing leaf + exclusive job ownership + no re-claim after cancellation).

(3) Consequence verified: every reachable transition where st.primary # NoError writes an identical value, so PrimaryStable (line 830) would hold even if the IF st.primary = NoError guards (lines 463, 472, 481) were replaced by unconditional overwrites — a last-exception-wins spec passes MC_Fail identically. Zero mutation adequacy. In MC_Normal/MC_PL1/MC_MultiWave/MC_NoSteal, FailLeaves={} and FaultySteps={} disable all fault actions, so PrimaryStable is antecedent-vacuous there. MC_Fail is the sole fault config (log line ~41: 4,385 generated / 1,852 distinct states).

(4) This is a contract violation, not a documented abstraction: requirement 8 makes first-exception-wins a verification obligation; the review mandate and the F1 precedent (requirement 3) ban exactly this hidden-vacuity pattern. The harness is asymmetric — verify_tla.sh builds a full negative-witness apparatus (MC_NoSteal) to prove ParticipationLive falsifiable but provides no falsifiability evidence for PrimaryStable — and MC_Fail's header (lines 4-5) affirmatively claims the run verifies "first-exception-wins", asserting coverage the state space cannot provide. The dead "eOther" constant underlines that distinct-error racing was intended but never made reachable.

(5) The suggested fix is live: with mc_FailLeaves == {1, 3}, block 1 (<<1, 3>>) populates leaf 1 (hash 1: Pass0=0, LeafOf=1) and leaf 3 (hash 3: Pass0=1, LeafOf=1); with WORKERS=2 both workers can concurrently own ProbeJob(1) and ProbeJob(3), FaultProbe has no ~cancelled guard, so the second fault attempts to write a DIFFERENT value (eL1 vs eOther) in either order — removing the guard would then yield a real PrimaryStable counterexample, making the check non-vacuous.

Refutation attempts all failed: no reachable cross-phase double fault (frozen phase after cancellation), no same-phase distinct-value pair (FailLeaves={1}, exclusive ownership), no multi-wave reopening (CompleteWave ~cancelled-guarded, and leaf 1 can never complete anyway), and no documented acknowledgment of the limitation (the opposite is claimed in MC_Fail's header). Severity: legitimate — the failure-path headline property ("first exception wins", contract item 8) is currently verified by a configuration that cannot distinguish first-wins from last-wins.

The factual claim is accurate but the finding is not a defect. Empirically confirmed: removing the `st.phase # "failed" =>` antecedent from `MemAccounted` (WaveJoinProbe.tla lines 636-637) and re-running TLC on MC_Fail yields "Model checking completed. No error has been found" with the identical 4,385/1,852 state counts as the gate log — the unscoped equality is a true invariant, exactly as the claimant argues (Teardown touches neither mem/queue/wk, its guard plus OwnershipConsistent conjunct 4 force InflightBytes=0, FaultScan/ReleaseRes subtract bytes atomically with clearing res, and the "failed" phase is frozen). However, by the binding criterion the finding is real only if the scoping violates the contract or hides vacuity, and it does neither: (1) F5's obligations are all discharged — MemAccounted covers every phase where accounting is live, CrossedSound covers the single atomic crossing, and MemBound (the required wave_bytes <= BUDGET + MaxBlockBytes bound) is checked unscoped including in "failed"; requirement 8's failure-path obligations are modeled via liveEntries/freedEntries/TerminalClean/FreedOnce, not mem. (2) No vacuity is hidden — MemAccounted is non-vacuously checked and falsifiable in all positive configs, and the excluded terminal region provably satisfies the predicate anyway, so no violation can hide behind the antecedent; the claimant concedes this verbatim ("The scope hides no violation — it merely under-claims"). (3) No soundness hole. What remains is a theorem-strength/style preference (check the strongest true invariant) plus an interpretive worry that the antecedent "falsely implies" desynchronization — but a scoped invariant asserts nothing about the excluded phase, and the review instructions restrict findings to contract failures, hidden vacuity, or soundness holes and explicitly exclude style nits. This is a defensible conservative scoping, not a defect.

CONFIRMED by exhaustive TLC run, not just reading. I copied the production spec and MC_Fail into tmp/verify-claim-work and model-checked MC_Fail's full state space (1852 distinct states) with invariants asserting the claimed-unreachable states: st.probeDone # Leaves, st.phase # "done", st.doneWaves = <<>>, and the EOFSeal pre-state never occurring — TLC reported "No error has been found", proving all four unreachability claims. Root cause verified in the sources: FinishProbe(w,1) is permanently disabled (WaveJoinProbe.tla:421, l \notin FailLeaves, with mc_FailLeaves = {1} and leaf 1 populated by hash 1), so CompleteWave (guard st.probeDone = Leaves at line 431) never fires in MC_Fail; both 1-byte blocks against BUDGET = 2 make crossed permanent, so EOFSeal is also unreachable; hence MC_Fail — the ONLY config with CancelAllowed = TRUE or non-empty FailLeaves/FaultySteps (all cfgs read) — never reaches "done", never completes a wave, and never runs Teardown with doneWaves # <<>>. MC_Normal/MC_PL1/MC_MultiWave complete but have all fault/cancel actions permanently disabled. Consequences against the binding contract: requirement 8 (model normal completion AND injected failure AND cancellation under the SAME machine, incl. multi-wave) and requirement 9 (safety for arbitrary interleavings) are satisfied only in spec text, never in checked state space — cancel racing CompleteWave/Seal boundary, cancel in an EOFSeal pre-state, and fault/cancel during wave 2 with doneWaves non-empty are generated by no configuration, so TerminalClean's failed-branch after a completed wave, Teardown's exactly-once release with doneWaves # <<>>, and OutputJustified under partial second-wave cancellation are vacuously verified. Concrete mutation escape: deleting ~st.cancelled from CompleteWave (line 430) or from EOFSeal leaves the entire green gate green (verified logically: CompleteWave unenabled in MC_Fail regardless; cancelled always FALSE elsewhere), so the gate cannot enforce the contract's "no new claims after cancellation" at the wave-completion boundary. Not a documented abstraction: MC_Fail's header documents all-behaviors-fail, but verify_tla.sh claims MC_Fail covers "external cancellation" with the full safety battery and nowhere acknowledges the completion x cancellation gap. Minor overstatement in the claim: the FinishInput ~cancelled guard specifically is NOT mutation-invisible (double FaultScan reaches its mutated pre-state and TerminalClean would catch it), but the claimed interleaving (cancel with FinishInput otherwise enabled) is still never generated, so the finding stands. Suggested MC_CancelRace config (CancelAllowed = TRUE, no faults, multi-wave input, disjunctive termination) is the correct fix.

The raw observations are accurate (lines 8/27-28 say "fetch-add"; Reserve at lines 250-262 is a conditional add guarded by st.mem < BUDGET; no rejected-add/rollback transient is modeled), but the finding fails the contract test. (1) Binding contract item 5 itself prescribes exactly the modeled semantics: "active wave below threshold until the single atomic crossing admission; bound like wave_bytes <= BUDGET + MAX_BLOCK_BYTES" — that bound is only consistent with single-crossing conditional-reservation accounting, so the spec matches the contract rather than violating it; the finding's option (b) (physical bound BUDGET + WORKERS*MaxBlockBytes) would deviate from requirement 5. (2) The abstraction is documented at the action itself: the comment at lines 245-249 states "Enabled only while the counter is below BUDGET; the addition that reaches or crosses BUDGET marks the wave crossed", so nothing is hidden — the residue is that the mapping phrase says "fetch-add" instead of "conditional add", a comment-wording nit (the finding's own minimal fix (a) is a comment edit), and style/doc nits are out of scope. (3) The verified MemBound does transfer to a literal fetch_add+rollback implementation under the standard refinement mapping mem = physical counter minus in-flight rejected adds: old < BUDGET implies logical sum < BUDGET (counter >= logical sum), successful adds are never rolled back so the logical sum crosses BUDGET exactly once, and reject+rollback pairs map to stutter; the transiently inflated physical counter is below the abstraction level exactly like the other excluded memory the header already disclaims (lines 36-42). (4) Seal (line 285) is conditioned on all workers' res = NoBlock, not a counter comparison, so "Seal reads the inflated counter" is speculation about an implementation refinement violation, not something the spec permits; the rollback obligations the contract does impose (item 8 failure/cancel unwinding) are modeled (FaultScan line 459, ReleaseRes lines 498-503) and checked via MemAccounted. (5) No vacuity: MC_ReachCross proves the overshoot region (crossed with in-flight reservation) reachable, per the green gate log. Net: a defensible, documented grain-of-atomicity abstraction plus an imprecise comment — not a contract failure, hidden vacuity, or soundness hole.

findings.claim: Refinement honesty is overstated: `FinishRefine` and `FinishProbe` launder scatter placement and duplication defects, so `FinalRefinement` is falsifiable only for presence/absence of occurrences (drops), while scatter stability and cross-wiring correctness are delegated entirely to `CellSafety`/`StableAtBarriers`/`RankInjective` — invariants that are correct-by-construction and cannot fail under any interleaving of the unmutated spec. The comments at src/Interpreters/RadixHashJoin/WaveJoinProbe.tla:387-389 ('read the ACTUAL pass-arena contents ... a scatter defect must propagate') and :736-738 ('no cross-wiring') claim propagation/coverage the checked refinement does not provide.
findings.evidence: src/Interpreters/RadixHashJoin/WaveJoinProbe.tla:392 — `occs == SeqSet(st.arena0[p]) \ {NoRow}` reads the pass arena as a SET, discarding cell positions and multiplicities; lines 400-403 recompute every arena1 target from canonical `Rank1(WaveRows, o)`, not from where `o` actually sat; line 425 — `FinishProbe` emits `ConcatResults(DropNoRow(st.arena1[l]))` where `RowResult(o)` depends only on the occurrence, never on leaf `l` or cell index, so a row in the wrong leaf/slot yields identical output. Mutation experiment (tmp/wave-join-review/mutA): reversing every pass arena at `ScatterBarrier` (a placement/stability defect) ran GREEN on `FinalRefinement`+`OutputJustified`+`Termination` over the full MC_Normal state space ('Model checking completed. No error has been found', identical 26,339/11,832 state counts — the mutation is a state-graph isomorphism invisible to the output path) and was caught only by `StableAtBarriers`. Counter-experiment (tmp/wave-join-review/mutB): dropping occurrence <<2,1>> in `FinishScatter` violated `FinalRefinement`, confirming only presence/absence propagates. In the unmutated spec, `CellSafety` (line 706), `StableAtBarriers` (722), `RankInjective` (696), `CapacityExact` (716) are theorems of the construction — every arena write derives both index and value from the same canonical `Pid`/`Lid`/`Rank0`/`Rank1` functions — so the invariants carrying the residual correctness have zero in-model checking power. F6's letter is satisfied (FinalRefinement checked by successful TLC configs, non-vacuously: with all cancellation sources disabled, `failed` is unreachable, so the checked `Termination` forces `done` to be reached), and the target `AllInputResults` plus `SeqCount` bag semantics are correct (cross-wave duplicate exercised in MC_MultiWave); the defect is that the spec's comments hide this partial vacuity by asserting defect classes propagate to refinement when they cannot.
findings.suggested_fix: Either make the output path positionally faithful — e.g. have `FinishRefine` iterate `arena0[p]` by actual index (deriving the arena1 slot from the stored sequence, not from canonical `Rank1`), and make `FinishProbe` emission depend on the (leaf, occurrence) pair so `Lid(o) # l` produces an observable wrong result — or fix the comments at lines 387-389 and 736-738 to state honestly: only occurrence loss/duplication propagates to `FinalRefinement`; scatter stability and leaf routing are definitional in this model and are documented (not checked) by `CellSafety`/`StableAtBarriers`.

findings.claim: Contract item 8's 'exactly-once release' is not falsifiably checked for the leaf arenas: `liveA1` releases are idempotent set removals with no `freedA1` counter under `FreedOnce`, so a double-release defect on a leaf arena is unrepresentable and undetectable, unlike the input entries and pass arenas which get monotone counters.
findings.evidence: src/Interpreters/RadixHashJoin/WaveJoinProbe.tla:746-748 — `FreedOnce == st.freedEntries <= 1 /\ st.freedA0 <= 1` covers only the wave input entries and the pass arenas. Leaf-arena release sites — `FinishProbe` line 426 (`!.liveA1 = @ \ {l}`), `FaultProbe` line 482 (`!.liveA1 = @ \ {l}`), `Teardown` line 524 (`!.liveA1 = {}`) — mutate a set, where removing an already-released leaf is a no-op. The spec deliberately instruments exactly-once freeing of the other two resources with counters checked by an invariant (lines 520-521 increment `freedEntries`/`freedA0` at `Teardown` guarded on non-emptiness precisely so a double free is countable), but the analogous instrumentation is absent for arena1, so that part of the release obligation is enforced by construction rather than by a checkable invariant.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a per-leaf release counter (e.g. `freedA1 \in [Leaves -> Nat]`, incremented by `FinishProbe`, `FaultProbe`, and by `Teardown` for each still-live leaf) and extend `FreedOnce` with `\A l \in Leaves : st.freedA1[l] <= 1`, mirroring the existing `freedEntries`/`freedA0` pattern.

result.reasoning: The cited facts are accurate (WaveJoinProbe.tla:583 permits five fault sites; MC_Fail.tla:24 enables only {"scan","pre"}; other configs use {}; MC_Fail explored 1,852 distinct states), but the gap does not violate the binding contract or hide vacuity. Requirement 8 requires modeling injected failure with first-exception-wins, unwind, exactly-once release, and valid terminal states — the harness checks injected failure at three sites (FaultScan, FaultStep-on-pre, FaultProbe) plus external cancellation; it never requires faults at every step kind. FaultStep (lines 465-472) is textually identical for all job kinds, and both components of the unexplored combination are independently exercised in MC_Fail: mid-scatter/refalloc/refine unwind (job released, done-set not updated, Teardown exactly-once release from those phases) is reached via ExternalCancel with FreedOnce/TerminalClean/OwnershipConsistent checked, and primary=FaultError-set-atomically-with-job-release is reached via the pre fault with PrimaryStable/FailureSafety checked; all primary-sensitive properties are phase-insensitive, so no checked property could differ on the missing combination and none passes vacuously because of it. The gate's coverage statement (verify_tla.sh:10) accurately scopes what MC_Fail checks — the claim itself concedes this. Extending mc_FaultySteps would be a cheap coverage-breadth improvement, but as reported this is a test-breadth nit against a documented, defensible checking scope, not a contract failure or soundness hole.

The claim's line citations are accurate (Footprint at WaveJoinProbe.tla:678-687 uses non-intersecting "a0" vs "a0cell" keys, and cross-kind co-ownership is unreachable via OwnershipConsistent conjunct 2 over phase-keyed ExistingJobs at lines 179-186/672-673), but the cited behavior violates no contract clause and hides no required non-vacuity. Contract requirement 3's non-vacuity demand is specific to the participation property (F1), discharged by ParticipationLive plus the MC_NoSteal witness, not by RaceFree. Requirement 4 permits "disjoint OR synchronized" write ranges: cross-kind exclusion is the synchronized arm, explicitly checked by the failable OwnershipConsistent conjunct 2 (TLC would flag a barrier firing over an owned stale job), so nothing is "silently delegated". RaceFree itself is not a tautology on reachable states: all co-ownable pairs are same-kind (phases serialize kinds), and for those pairs footprint keys do collide where writes collide — scatter-vs-scatter share the "a0cell" keyspace (disjointness genuinely depends on RankInjective; a buggy Rank0 would fail RaceFree) and refalloc/refine share <<"a1", l>> keys; MC_ReachOwn proves full co-ownership states are reachable, so the check is exercised. The claim's only harm scenario is a hypothetical future relaxation of the phase structure; the suggested fix would produce bit-identical TLC results on every configuration, the signature of a robustness/style nit rather than a defect. The claim itself concedes the mismatched branch is dead — it is semantically equivalent to the OTHER -> {} arm — and the spec documents the within-kind disjointness rationale (lines 330-332) while never advertising cross-kind footprint coverage. A defensible abstraction with an unreachable dead branch, not a contract failure, hidden vacuity, or soundness hole.

The cited facts are accurate (FreedOnce at WaveJoinProbe.tla:746-748 omits liveA1; releases at lines 426, 482, 524 are idempotent set operations), but the defect claim fails because exactly-once leaf-arena release is not "enforced only by construction": any per-leaf release requires ownership of ProbeJob(l), and double acquisition is excluded by the checked falsifiable invariant OwnershipConsistent (lines 670-673: unique job ownership plus owned-job membership in ExistingJobs, which excludes probeDone at line 185). A double FinishProbe would additionally duplicate emitted results and trip the checked OutputJustified (line 732) and FinalRefinement. So the realistic double-release defect class IS representable and detectable via two independent checked invariants. The counter asymmetry is a documented, rationale-backed abstraction: freedEntries/freedA0 instrument bulk output-silent frees with two release sites (barrier + Teardown), whereas leaf release is fused to a uniquely-owned single-shot job with observable output; Teardown's liveA1 clear is the documented "release what is still live" sweep (lines 512-513) and Teardown cannot fire twice. The binding contract's non-vacuity requirement (item 3) is scoped to the participation property (F1), not every obligation, and item 8's exactly-once release holds in every behavior with leak-freedom checked by TerminalClean. The suggested freedA1 counter is optional mutation-hardening, not a contract failure, hidden vacuity, or soundness hole.

All cited facts check out in src/Interpreters/RadixHashJoin/WaveJoinProbe.tla: FreedOnce (lines 746-748) bounds only st.freedEntries and st.freedA0; those counters are incremented at ScatterBarrier (lines 360/367), RefineBarrier (line 413) and Teardown (lines 520-521, with IF-nonempty guards showing the author deliberately modeled the already-freed-at-teardown case for those two resource classes). Leaf arenas have no counter anywhere (Init lines 237-241, TypeOK lines 627-631, CompleteWave resets only freedEntries/freedA0) and are released by idempotent set operations: FinishProbe line 426 and FaultProbe line 482 use `!.liveA1 = @ \ {l}`, Teardown line 524 uses `!.liveA1 = {}`. I attempted refutation by walking the entire checked battery: CapacityExact and the arena invariants quantify only over members of liveA1 (weaker after a spurious removal), StableAtBarriers constrains arena1 contents which FinishProbe never clears, TerminalClean requires liveA1 = {} so extra releases only help it, and no invariant ties liveA1 to probeDone. The strongest counter-argument — that leaf release exactly-once is subsumed by probe-completion exactly-once (OwnershipConsistent + OutputJustified) — only covers double-release via double-completion; release-accounting errors decoupled from completion (early clear, teardown re-free, FaultProbe/Teardown overlap) are exactly the class the freedEntries/freedA0 counters were purpose-built to catch for the other two resource classes, and for liveA1 they are structurally undetectable because set removal is a state no-op. The spec does not document this as an abstraction; instead its comments assert the unverifiable claim ("The leaf arena is released exactly once, here", lines 417-418; "each resource exactly once", Teardown comment), and all four positive TLC configs check FreedOnce and pass, so the green gate presents exactly-once release as verified when one of the three resource classes is uncovered. This hides vacuity with respect to contract requirement 8 (exactly-once release). It is a verification-coverage hole rather than a reachable-behavior bug (no reachable behavior double-frees, and requirement 3's explicit non-vacuity wording targets the participation property), which is consistent with the claimed medium severity. The suggested fix (per-leaf freedA1 counters at the three release sites, extending FreedOnce, reset in CompleteWave because leaves are reused across waves) is coherent with the existing idiom.

The logical observation is verified correct: in src/Interpreters/RadixHashJoin/WaveJoinProbe.tla, Termination (line 801) implies ParticipationLive (lines 821-826) on every behavior — at terminal phases ExistingJobs = {} (line 186 OTHER) and ScanOpen is false (line 809 requires phase = "active"), terminal phases are absorbing, so the escape disjunct eventually-always holds; and MC_NoSteal's broken_ClaimEligible does orphan ProbeJob(0) (worker 0 barred from all claims, leaf 0 barred to all others), so the witness is a non-terminating wedge that would violate Termination as well. All completing positive configs check both properties, so the redundancy-where-checked observation is factually accurate. However, this does not violate the binding contract or hide vacuity. (1) Requirement 3's stated criteria are met — the claim itself concedes this: WorkAvailable compares ExistingJobs-derived work (phase + done-sets + queue only, line 179) against wk-derived ownership, and the property is demonstrably capable of failing (TLC reports a real temporal violation on MC_NoSteal in the green gate log). The F1 defect (a definitional tautology true of any spec) is genuinely fixed. (2) The stronger property the finding demands — one that fails on a work-conserving dedicated-crew design — is impossible in linear-time semantics: every fair trace of a terminating lazy-worker/static-partition/sealer-drains-alone design is a fair trace of the contractual spec (ClaimEligible == TRUE permits any restricted claiming pattern; WF is vacuously satisfied once enablement ends at termination), and trace-subset designs satisfy every temporal property the spec satisfies. Absence of an impossible property cannot be a defect. (3) Implication-by-Termination is therefore forced on any sound formulation: the consumed-by-others escape is necessary (under WF a worker may legitimately lose every claim race, so a per-worker property without it would be false of the correct design), and any such escape-carrying liveness property can only be violated by work persisting forever, i.e., non-termination. The contract requires non-vacuity ("capable of failing"), not logical independence from Termination; a redundant-but-sound property does not reduce what the verification catches. (4) Nothing is hidden: the spec documents the escape explicitly (lines 803-807), and both the spec header (lines 44-50) and verify_tla.sh (line 16) claim only falsifiability, which is accurate. The one genuine inaccuracy — "it fails exactly on dedicated-crew designs" in tmp/wave-join-cooperative/tla/MC_NoSteal.tla line 10, where "exactly" should be "on dedicated-crew designs that orphan work" — is a single-word comment overclaim in a tmp/ harness module, i.e., a documentation nit (the finding's own "at minimum" fix), not a contract failure, hidden vacuity, or soundness hole.

The claim's mechanics are all verified accurate: FinishRefine (WaveJoinProbe.tla:392) reads arena0 as a set via SeqSet, discarding position/multiplicity; arena1 targets are recomputed from canonical Rank1 (lines 400-403); FinishProbe output (line 425) is leaf-independent. The mutation artifacts check out: mutA (arena reversal at ScatterBarrier) is invisible to FinalRefinement+OutputJustified+Termination over the full MC_Normal space (identical 26,339/11,832 state counts) and is caught only by StableAtBarriers; mutB (dropped occurrence) violates FinalRefinement. So only presence/count defects propagate to the refinement, and placement/routing correctness is carried by CellSafety/StableAtBarriers.

But this does not violate the binding contract or hide vacuity. (a) F6 requires only that FinalRefinement be checked by a successful TLC config — satisfied non-vacuously (done is forced reachable; mutB proves falsifiability). (b) Contract item 7 DEFINES correctness as exact output multiset equality with order unconstrained — FinalRefinement is exactly that definition, so multiset-preserving permutations are outside the contract's own correctness criterion. (c) Item 3's non-vacuity demand is explicitly scoped to the participation property (F1), discharged by the MC_NoSteal witness; nothing requires scatter defects to propagate to FinalRefinement. (d) The "zero checking power / correct-by-construction" argument mischaracterizes vacuity: F1 was a definitional tautology incapable of failing in any model, whereas StableAtBarriers/CellSafety compare reached states to independently computed expectations and were falsified by the claimant's own one-line mutation (mutA2, violation at 70 states). "Cannot fail in the unmutated spec" is true of every invariant of a correct spec. These invariants have real in-model power against the error class TLA+ exists for — interleaving/barrier defects (e.g. admission mid-drain or refine overlapping scatter would fail them). (e) The gate as shipped checks the full 19-invariant Safety battery (incl. StableAtBarriers, CellSafety) in every positive config, and jointly catches BOTH offered mutation classes — nothing is laundered by the harness, and verify_tla.sh never attributes scatter-mutation coverage to FinalRefinement. What survives is that two comment glosses (line 388 "a scatter defect must propagate", line 738 "no cross-wiring") are imprecise about which checked property covers which defect class, while the properties that do cover them are stated and checked immediately adjacent. That is a comment-wording precision issue in a documented, defensible abstraction — not a contract failure, not hidden vacuity, not a soundness hole — and fails the review's own bar for a reportable finding (let alone medium severity). If the team wants, tightening the two comments per the suggested fix's second option is a harmless polish, but the finding as claimed is not real.
